sc.quote: Raggies Cave Max. Depth: 14m-18m … Raggies Cave consists of, you guessed it, caves, gullies, swim-through, and overhangs, and the site is home to a variety of hard coral species as well as juvenile fish, false stonefish, scorpionfish and without a doubt Raggies in the winter months

bs.quote: Raggie's Cave Depth: 12-19 meters Look for: Ragged-tooth sharks … T&C: No one may dive into the cave when sharks are residing

ag.quote: Raggie Cave Maximum depth 17m. Best for Ragged- Tooth Sharks (during season)

hazards.text: Cave off limits while sharks are resting inside

summary.text: Cave, gully and overhang system on the seaward side of Aliwal Shoal, famed as the winter gathering spot of ragged-tooth sharks. Dives reach roughly 18 m and the rock is dotted with hard corals, juvenile fish and well-camouflaged scorpionfish.

sc.quote: North Sands Max. Depth: 12m-18m Another dive with a 17m maximum depth … This dive site is home to a ridiculous amount of round ribbontail rays … North Sands is also home to guitar sharks during the summer months

bs.quote: North Sands Depth: 15-17 meters Look for: Round ribbon-tail rays, guitar sharks, sole, shark’s teeth

highlights.text: Round ribbontail rays on the sand patch

summary.text: A large sand patch on the northern part of Aliwal Shoal ringed by reef. Reaching about 17 m, it is a place to look for ribbontail rays buried in the sand, summer guitar sharks, and old shark teeth lying among the shells.

sc.quote: South Sands Max. Depth: 14m-18m South Sands is another big sand patch dive spot with some reef which is home to box fish, puffer fish, crayfish, leather coral

bs.quote: South Sands Depth: 12-18 meters Look for: Like North Sands, this site is home to rays, skates, sand sharks and guitar sharks. The average depth is 15m with a maximum of 18m

ag.quote: South Sands Maximum depth 17m. Best for spotting large groups of rays, including sandsharks and pods of dolphins

highlights.text: Groups of rays, sand sharks and guitar sharks
Boxfish, pufferfish and leather coral on the reef

summary.text: Another sandy clearing on Aliwal Shoal with patches of reef around it, about 17-18 m deep. Rays, sand sharks and guitar sharks are the draw, with boxfish, crayfish and leather coral on the rock edges.

sc.quote: Cathedral Max. Depth: 18m-27m The deepest dive, Cathedral is a 27m max depth dive spot featuring a cave surrounded by crater-like rock formations. With all the ragged-tooth sharks patrolling the area

ag.quote: Cathedral Maximum depth 27m. Best for Ragged-Tooth Shark (during season) … Large amphitheatre structure with entrance either via large front archway, through the roof or through the swim through slightly to the side of the front archway

highlights.text: Crater-like amphitheatre with archway and swim-through

summary.text: Amphitheatre-shaped rock formation on the outer shoal, reached by a front archway, a roof opening or a side swim-through. It sits near 27 m, so it suits experienced divers, and ragged-tooth sharks often patrol it.

sc.quote: Chunnel Max. Depth: 10m-14m The Chunnel dive spot, also with a max diving depth of 17m, is the known waterway where the sharks are constantly on the move

bs.quote: Chunnel Depth: 12-17 meters Look for: Cave, turtles, sand sharks, ribbon-tail rays … Chunnel, which is near Raggies’ Cave, was named as such because it is a waterway where sharks constantly move

highlights.text: Turtles, sand sharks and ribbontail rays

summary.text: A shark-traffic channel close to Raggies Cave on Aliwal Shoal, about 17 m at most. Ragged-tooth sharks pass through constantly, with turtles, sand sharks and rays on the neighbouring sand; coral is sparse because of current.

sc.quote: Northern Pinnacles Max. Depth: 6m-17m … Reaching amazing heights of only 6m from the surface, this dive, with a maximum depth of 17m, has gullies, overhangs, caves and swim-throughs

bs.quote: Pinnacles Depth: 11-17 meters Look for: The potholes, manta rays, potato bass

ag.quote: Northern Pinnacles Maximum depth 18m … Top spot for Manta’s during the season

summary.text: A spine of rock formations rising to about 6 m below the surface at the north end of Aliwal Shoal, cut by gullies, potholes and swim-throughs. Mantas, rays and potato bass are regular sightings and the depth tops out near 17-18 m.

sc.quote: Eel Skin Max. Depth: 16m-22m … Eel Skin is home to starfish in every shape and size imaginable; as well as boasting peacock mantis shrimp, puffer fish, box fish, green fern coral and nudibranchs

bs.quote: Eelskins Depth: 18 meters Look for: Sharks, rays, mantas (summer), whale sharks (summer), dolphins(sometimes), reef fish, macro … Ocean erosion has shaped with part of the reef in gullies and overhangs and swim-throughs

summary.text: Eroded sandstone reef on Aliwal Shoal with gullies, overhangs and swim-throughs, down to roughly 18-22 m. Photographers like it for starfish, nudibranchs and peacock mantis shrimp, and ragged-tooth sharks drift in during winter.

cd.quote: Antons … Depth: 13-16m Qualification Required: Open Water

am.quote: Anton’s Cave Depth: 16-17m (OW Dive) … First discovered by early dive operator Anton Buchel, it has a high profile, and large shoals of Humpback, Bluebanded and Yellow snappers are always present

summary.text: High-profile ridge at the southern tip of Two Mile Reef that fills with snapper schools, fed by nutrient-rich north-south currents. About 16 m deep and open to Open Water divers, with morays, turtles and frogfish among the rocks.

cd.quote: 4 Buoy … A significant overhang doubles as a bustling cleaning station and a cosy habitat for the intriguing Honeycomb moray eel … Depth: 9-12m Qualification Required: Open Water

highlights.text: Overhang cleaning station with honeycomb morays

cd.quote: Bikini … Depth: 18-22m Qualification Required: Advanced Open Water … Divers are treated to exquisite sightings of Ghost and Scribbled Pipefish, alongside the serpentine sway of Garden eels

am.quote: Bikini Depth: 20-22m (ADV Dive) … The drop for this dive site is onto ‘Bikini Ledge’, where you are likely to see a large school of Schooling coachman and a small cave

highlights.text: Coachman school and small cave on Bikini Ledge

summary.text: Macro-friendly 2 Mile Reef dive that drops onto a ledge near 20-22 m. Expect schools of coachman, a small cave, garden eels and pipefish, and it is rated for Advanced Open Water divers.

cd.quote: Stringer … Depth: 10-13m Qualification Required: Open Water

am.quote: Stringer Depth: 09-13m (OW Dive) … Stringer, the southernmost dive site on 2 Mile, features twin rocky outcrops teeming with life. Best dived with minimal current and no surge

hazards.text: Best only with little current and no surge

summary.text: Twin rocky outcrops at the south end of Two Mile Reef, shallow at about 9-13 m. Good for Open Water divers on calm days, with frogfish, rays and morays on the rocks.

cd.quote: Ribbon … Depth: 16-19m Qualification Required: Advanced Open Water … named after the rare Ribbon eel often spotted around its periphery

am.quote: Ribbon Reef is a slightly larger and deeper version of Stringer, with a depth of 16m. Also comprised of two rocky outcrops, it is a firm favourite with macro photographers

summary.text: Two small rocky outcrops on Five Mile Reef, similar to Stringer but larger and deeper at 16-19 m. A favourite with macro photographers for ribbon eels, scorpionfish and anemones, with blacktip sharks and turtles often around.

cd.quote: Mellow Yellow … Nestled at the southern tip of Bikini, this site features a captivating narrow reef sprinkled with gullies, overhangs, and ledges … Depth: 16-18m Qualification Required: Open Water

am.quote: Mellow Yellow Depth: 18-20m (OW Dive) … Named for the large schools of yellow fish species seen here, this southern end of Bikini is a flat ribbon of reef with great ‘macro’ photography opportunities

summary.text: Narrow reef strip at the southern end of Bikini, about 16-20 m deep and open to Open Water divers. Named for its yellow-fish schools, it also offers gullies, overhangs and plenty of shrimp and nudibranch macro subjects.

cd.quote: Hopscotch mesmerises divers with its unique topography of scattered ledges and homey crannies for elusive Ribbon Eels and camouflaged Frogfish … Depth: 22-25m Qualification Required: Advanced Open Water

highlights.text: Ribbon eels and frogfish in ledges

cd.quote: Roonies is a diver’s delight, stationed off the coast of 2 Mile … including the territorial Long Nose Hawkfish and the resident Seahorse … Depth: 27-32m Qualification Required: Advanced Open Water

summary.text: Compact deeper site off Two Mile Reef at roughly 27-32 m, requiring Advanced Open Water. Small and busy, it is known for a resident seahorse and longnose hawkfish.

cd.quote: World, a standout amongst Sodwana Bay reefs, offers a slightly deeper adventure with its flat terrain, making it perfect for those interested in drift dives … A special highlight is the enchanting turtle cave … Depth: 14-16 m Qualification Required: Open Water

sd.quote: the gullies at Wayne’s World (filled with Raggies in summer)

highlights.text: Raggies in the gullies in summer

summary.text: Flat, slightly deeper section of Two Mile Reef (14-16 m) that suits drift dives. Soft corals and a turtle cave are the highlights, and ragged-tooth sharks gather in its gullies in summer.

cd.quote: Coral Gardens is renowned for its rich tapestry of hard and soft corals, presenting a flat topography that makes it ideal for drift dives, especially in stronger currents … Depth: 10-13m Qualification Required: Open Water

Deep Sponge offers a rare spectacle, nestled parallel to 2 Mile Reef, about 500m off the coast. It’s distinguished by its magnificent, vase-shaped sponges … Depth: 28-32m Qualification Required: Advanced Open Water
